scope: Post-score targeted review of two fixed16 interventions, with eight native-resolution frames and all32 actual AutoEval sampling frames; not a random sample or a full-suite visual verdict.

cases.normal: The wood-like material becomes broad loose/ribbon-like shapes and overlaps or deforms the people; the requested coherent bending is not established.
cases.wrong: Every one of the32 frames selected by the existing AutoEval loader (indices1..79) is dominated by repeated texture/noise; the intended people/wood scene is not coherently represented. The fixed frame0 remains recognizable.
cases.interpretation: PC5 is a clear score/visual-quality conflict here. It cannot be treated as improved physical execution under wrong reasoning, and the normal video is also visibly defective.

cases.normal: The sampled normal sequence develops a periodic surface texture; the roller later narrows and disappears without establishing a clean paint-transfer process.
cases.wrong: From roughly frame11 the cylindrical roller becomes a broad sheet-like object, later appearing disconnected or discontinuous relative to its handle.
cases.interpretation: This sole new Joint pass under wrong reasoning does not establish visibly correct rolling/paint-transfer mechanics. Both arms retain notable defects.

quantitative_decomposition.scope: Describe contributions without deleting cases, replacing scores or reporting a modified benchmark.

decision: Retain all original benchmark outputs. Correct-reasoning benefit remains unproven, and wrong-reasoning mean gain is not evidence of better generation. New candidate selection must consider visual failures alongside matched scores; no blanket claim that all AutoEval results are invalid.
next_architecture_implication: Potential conditioning/write instability deserves attention if reproduced in normal revised-data outputs; wrong-condition failure alone does not identify its source or justify an untested numerical patch. Keep submitted new R11A unchanged until its own results.

official_protocol_check.result: No evidence of a first-frame-only read, wrong frame-count setting, or score parsing error for these two outputs. This does not audit all evaluator internals.
